h: Planning your raid on the armoury
p: The museum opened in Leeds in 1996, bringing much of the Royal Armouries' famous collection up from the Tower of London to a purpose-built home by the water. It's grown into one of the city's best-loved days out.

Allow a few hours to explore properly. With five floors to cover, it's worth grabbing a map and picking out a few must-sees, then letting the rest unfold as you go. Check the day's programme of live interpretations and demonstrations when you arrive, because they're a highlight and it's a shame to miss them.

Families can make it into a game: hunt for the most outrageous helmet, the biggest weapon or the most dazzling piece of decoration. Kids who love knights, samurai and castles will be in their element, and grown-ups often find themselves just as hooked.
Getting there is simple. It's a pleasant walk from Leeds railway station along the River Aire, and there's parking nearby if you're driving.

Afterwards, Leeds city centre has plenty more to explore. The Victoria Quarter is famous for its beautiful Victorian arcades, Kirkgate Market is a huge covered market that is great for food, and the Corn Exchange is a striking domed building full of independent shops. Leeds Minster sits close to the dock, a fine historic church that's worth a peek on your way back into town.
